The fiber lengths are very uniform for both 1” and ½”. However, it can be seen that the fiber width varied for different fiber lengths. The 1” fiber length, had fiber width 0.02” to 0.14” since not all of the fiber deagglomerates. The sizing has an effect of keeping the filaments together and the fiber-cutter interaction forces and fall under gravity were not sufficient to fully filamentize (deagglomerate) the 600k Kaltex TCF. Yet the 1” fiber had significant filamentization when compared to the ½” fiber (Figure 32 versus Figure 33). The fiber width for the ½” fiber length varied from 0.02” to 0.23” which is almost twice that of the 1”. This can also be seen visually in Figure 33. It appears that as the fiber length gets shorter, there is less fiber compliance and hence the tendency is to stay together. 1.2 1 0.8 0.6 0.4 0.2 0 Length Figure 32.
